## Season Changes[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   For this season only, [Mike Richards](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Mike_Richards "Mike Richards") was the executive producer of both _Jeopardy!_ and _Wheel of Fortune_.
*   [Ken Jennings](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Ken_Jennings "Ken Jennings") became consulting producer beginning with this season.
*   During this season, various changes are made to the set: 
    *   The contestant lecterns are spaced six feet apart from one another, and are now separate pieces. 
        *   Despite pandemic restrictions being lifted in Season 39, the spacing of the lecterns is made permanent because it fits perfectly inside a 16:9 ratio frame. When the lecterns were one large set piece, they were optimized more for 4:3.
        *   The backdrop on the contestant's lecterns are now blue for regular shows.

    *   The host's lectern and the large monitor next to it are redesigned, the latter is now mounted on two brown posts.
    *   The background is changed to a dark blue color scheme.
    *   The curved shapes became a lavender and a maroon color, and the pillar was removed from the set.
    *   There are two golden arches on the stage floor, one is near the game board, and the other one near the contestant lecterns. These are carried over from the Greatest of All Time.

*   The opening credits have changed to a redesigned version of the globe logo. The globe zooms in, and we see photographs and footage from the show. Finally, the photographs and footage disappear, and the white _Jeopardy!_ logo zooms out with a blue globe with peach land lights behind it on a blue space background. Then, the _Jeopardy!_ logo zooms forward, in which the "A" reveals the revamped 2013-present set.
*   The Daily Double, Video Daily Double, and split-screen credits gained a new look to match the season's title card.
*   The gameplay round title cards now feature the "DOUBLE" and "FINAL" in _Double_ and _Final Jeopardy!_ just in white, using the Trade Gothic Std Bold font which continues to be used as of now.
*   However, the _Double_ and _Final Jeopardy!_ backdrops look different than the title card without the globe and with pink spotlights added to the blue sky background as well as Daily Doubles.
*   The copyright and "Created by Merv Griffin" credits is now changed to a blue starry color scheme with gold bars and it continues to be used as of now.
*   Beginning with this season, the camera views are changed during the thinking period in _Final Jeopardy!_. The camera still pans along the floor from the stage front to the contestant podiums. However, the camera now shows full shots of all three lecterns in-between close-ups of the contestants. After the close-up of the middle contestant, the camera pans downwards slightly while showing all three lecterns at an angle before changing to a close-up of the rightmost contestant. This is due to the podiums being spaced farther apart than in earlier seasons.
*   This is the first season to be produced by Sony Pictures Television Studios until the end of Season 39.
*   For both this season and the next season, the [Jeopardy! Clue Crew](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Jeopardy!_Clue_Crew "Jeopardy! Clue Crew"), which consisted of [Sarah Whitcomb-Foss](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Sarah_Whitcomb-Foss "Sarah Whitcomb-Foss") and [Jimmy McGuire](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Jimmy_McGuire "Jimmy McGuire"), presented clues less often due to travel restrictions in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, featuring clues that were filmed prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.
*   On early episodes of this season: 
    *   The show was still hosted by [Alex Trebek](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Alex_Trebek "Alex Trebek").
    *   The show was still distributed by CBS Television Distribution.
    *   Selected episodes featured Ken Jennings providing entire video clue categories.

*   This is the first season to be distributed by CBS Media Ventures.
*   This is also the first season since Season 2 to have only one tournament held.
*   This is the only season to have the revolving guest host format.
*   This is the last season for the following: 
    *   The 2008-2021 theme is used since Season 25.
    *   Johnny says "Jeopardy! is also brought to you by..." since Season 34 and "promotional consideration provided by..." after the host signs off since Season 16.
    *   CBS Television Distribution distributing the show since Season 24.
    *   The promotional fee plugs in the closing credits.
    *   The tournament to have (semi)finalist for the winner of the quarterfinal or semifinal games.
    *   The last Tournament of Champions to use a two-day total point affair in the finals. Starting next Tournament of Champions, it will use a best of seven series.
    *   The show's taping location is known as Sony Pictures Studios Stage 10. It was renamed as The Alex Trebek Stage the following season in honor of Alex's legacy.
    *   Full season where Johnny Gilbert's catchphrase is "This is Jeopardy!". Starting on the second episode of next season, Johnny Gilbert's catchphrase is changed to "From the Alex Trebek Stage at Sony Pictures Studios, this is _Jeopardy!_."
    *   John Lauderdale as the stage manager, as he retired at the end of this season.
    *   Full season with Clay Jacobsen as the director.
    *   Alex Trebek as the host since the syndicated series premiered on September 10, 1984.
    *   Third season in the show's history and the last time in the Alex Trebek era where the reigning champion did not return.
    *   Episodes in the Alex Trebek era where two of the three Daily Doubles are seen on time.
    *   GEICO sponsors the consolation prizes since Season 34.

*   The Teachers Tournament and the College Championship are not held this season due to rotating guest hosts and COVID-19.
*   This is the third occurrence where no champions coming from this season who participated in the Tournament of Champions made it to the finals.
*   This is the first season since Season 30 to end its original run in August, rather than July.
*   Filming began on July 28, 2020, and the last show of the season was filmed on May 4, 2021.
*   Last season in which the camera briefly shows a dollar amount that isn't the lowest or highest valued amount ($400, $600, $800 in the Jeopardy! round; $800, $1200, $1600 in Double Jeopardy!) when they select a clue.
*   First and only season in which the zoomed-in dollar values are only shown when the contestants are playing categories top to bottom.
*   This is also the only season to use the 2nd version of the 2013-present set before undergoing further modifications in Season 38.

## September 2020[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D3&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **September 14, 2020**: Season 37 begins. On the season premiere, there are three new contestants. It is the third time in the show's history and the last time in the Alex Trebek era where the reigning champion did not return. [Zach Newkirk](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Zach_Newkirk "Zach Newkirk"), an attorney from Alexandria, Virginia, was unable to return until January 28, 2021 as a co-champion due to travel restrictions in wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. Alex said a few weeks time.
*   **September 16, 2020**: Kelly Decker is the first contestant without a audience to be disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round with -$1,400.
*   **September 21, 2020**: Two of the three Daily Doubles are seen on time.

## October 2020[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **October 13, 2020**: This is the sixth time, only one contestant (Kevin Walsh) participated in the _Final Jeopardy!_ round, this is the last time a single-player _Final Jeopardy!_ round played in the Alex Trebek era. This was on his fourth game. Alex Switzky is disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round with $0 and Natt Supab is disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round in the red with -$400. Alex's dismissal comes after he missed the Daily Double, found on the Double Jeopardy round's clue before the Beeps of Time, while risking all his winnings.
*   **October 15, 2020**: [Kevin Walsh](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Kevin_Walsh "Kevin Walsh") finishes with a 5-day total of $111,301, and was also the last 5-time champion whose streak aired during Alex Trebek's life. He is defeated by Kristin Hucek in a come from behind win.
*   **October 16, 2020**: Aanchal Ramani is disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round in the red with -$200.
*   **October 20, 2020**: Kristin Hucek is the last woman champion in the Alex Trebek era to be disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round in the red with -$3,600.
*   **October 28, 2020**: The last episode in the Alex Trebek era where two of the three Daily Doubles are seen on time. Jennifer Spinos is the last woman contestant in the Alex Trebek era to be disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round in the red with -$400.

## November 2020[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D5&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   This is the first season since Season 1 to not have any tournaments held in November.
*   **November 6, 2020**: This episode marked the final episode aired before Alex Trebek's death. It was also the last time where the 2008-2021 theme music ends at the same time as the credits.
*   **November 8, 2020**: [Alex Trebek](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Alex_Trebek "Alex Trebek") died at the age of 80 from pancreatic cancer, his spirit and television legacy live on.
*   **November 9, 2020**: This episode marked the first episode aired after Alex Trebek's death. It was also the first time where the closing theme ends mid-theme since Season 13. 
    *   Executive producer Mike Richards pays tribute to Alex Trebek at the beginning of the show.
    *   A dedication card is used for the first time reading: "Dedicated to Alex Trebek, forever in our hearts, always our Inspiration," which was used for the rest of the season.

*   **November 18, 2020**: [Deanna Bolio](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Deanna_Bolio "Deanna Bolio") finishes in third with $10,399.
*   **November 20, 2020**: [Andy Wood](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Andy_Wood "Andy Wood") finishes with a 4-day total of $91,999 after Alex Trebek's death, where he was defeated by Charlie Fonville.
*   **November 26, 2020**: Last game in the Alex Trebek era to have a all male game.

## December 2020[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D6&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **December 1, 2020**: [Ryan Hemmel](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Ryan_Hemmel "Ryan Hemmel") finishes with a 4-day total of $104,526, where he is defeated by T.J. Tallie.
*   **December 15, 2020**: [Brayden Smith](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Brayden_Smith "Brayden Smith") makes his _Jeopardy!_ debut.
*   **December 21, 2020-January 1, 2021**: Jeopardy! Around the World airs, featuring reruns of Alex's favorite traveling-themed episodes. 
    *   **October 14, 2004** episode (#4624) from Season 21, where Alex presents some hockey-themed video clues with Tie Domi from the Toronto Maple Leafs, was repeated on December 21, 2020. The 2001 theme is plastered by the 2008 theme during the closing credits.
    *   **April 4, 2006** episode (#4972) from Season 22, where Alex presents some clues with the cast of Sesame Street, was repeated on December 22, 2020.
    *   **September 27, 2007** episode (#5299) from Season 24, where Alex traveled to Kadena Air Force Base in Japan, was repeated on December 23, 2020.
    *   **November 6, 2007** episode (#5327) from Season 24, where Alex traveled to Machu Picchu in Peru, was repeated on December 24, 2020.
    *   **January 15, 2009** episode (#5609) from Season 25, where Alex traveled to Niagara Falls was repeated on December 25, 2020.

## January 2021[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D7&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **January 4-8, 2021**: Alex Trebek's final episodes aired, originally scheduled for December 21-25, 2020. 
    *   **January 5, 2021**: [Brayden Smith](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Brayden_Smith "Brayden Smith")'s streak ends, with a 5-day total of $115,798, where he was defeated by Manisha Munshi, making him the last five-time champion in the Alex Trebek era. Sadly, he tragically passed away a month later on February 5, 2021 at the age of 24 due to complications following surgery.
    *   **January 7, 2021**: 
        *   Last game where all clues are shown in every round in the Alex Trebek era.
        *   Last game in the Alex Trebek era to have a all female game.
        *   Last episode where all three contestants play _Final Jeopardy!_ in the Alex Trebek era.

    *   **January 8, 2021**: Alex Trebek's final episode aired. It concluded with a tribute montage, featuring Alex's most memorable moments. The song used in the tribute was the song "Once Before I Go" from the 2003 musical _The Boy From Oz_. Last game in the Alex Trebek era where clues went unplayed. Cliff Chang is the last contestant in the Alex Trebek era to be disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round with -$400. Jim Gilligan becomes the last new champion in the Alex Trebek era.

*   **January 11, 2021-August 13, 2021**: _Jeopardy!_ used the guest host and guest hostess format, famous celebrities, journalists, and former _Jeopardy!_ contestants host. Each guest host is announced by Johnny Gilbert as "The guest host of _Jeopardy!_"
*   **January 11-February 19, 2021**: _Jeopardy!_ champion and consulting producer [Ken Jennings](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Ken_Jennings "Ken Jennings") hosted. 
    *   **January 11, 2021**: 
        *   The opening graphics are changed to remove footage of [Alex Trebek](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Alex_Trebek "Alex Trebek").
        *   First game where all clues are shown in every round in the post-Trebek era.

    *   **January 14, 2021**: The first game in the post-Trebek era where clues went unplayed.
    *   **January 15, 2021**: [Lucy Ricketts](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Lucy_Ricketts "Lucy Ricketts") finishes with a 3-day total of $79,499. The CBS Television Distribution logo appears for the last time since the September 27, 2007 episode of Season 24.
    *   **January 18, 2021**: The CBS Media Ventures logo appears for the first time, and it has a ViacomCBS byline.
    *   **January 19, 2021**: [Brian Chang](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Brian_Chang "Brian Chang") makes his _Jeopardy!_ debut.
    *   **January 22, 2021**: This is the third time a tie-breaker clue was played during regular play in the _Final Jeopardy!_ round. It was also the first time a Tiebreaker round was played in the post-Trebek era. On this episode, [Brian Chang](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Brian_Chang "Brian Chang") won his 4th game.
    *   **January 28, 2021**: [Brian Chang](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Brian_Chang "Brian Chang") was defeated by [Zach Newkirk](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Zach_Newkirk "Zach Newkirk"), finishing with a 7-day total of $163,904. It was also the third instance to feature returning co-champions as a rare occurrence only applying to champions previously unable to return, and the second time after the co-champion rule was disestablished early in Season 31. Brian is also the first champion in the post-Trebek era to qualify for the Tournament of Champions.

## February 2021[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D8&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **February 1, 2021**: [Zach Newkirk](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Zach_Newkirk "Zach Newkirk") finishes with a 6-day total of $124,871, where he is defeated by Steve Crupi in a come from behind win. [Ken Jennings](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Ken_Jennings "Ken Jennings") stated that his streak ended after the eligibility closed for this Tournament of Champions. As a result, he was carried over to the next Tournament of Champions.
*   **February 5, 2021**: [Brayden Smith](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Brayden_Smith "Brayden Smith") dies at age 24, a month after he lost his streak.
*   **February 12, 2021**: [John Focht](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/John_Focht "John Focht") finishes with 4-day total of $103,800, where he was defeated by Lance St. Laurent.
*   After the February 12, 2021 episode, there were no 5-time champ in 100 regular games. Also, during 37 games, there was not even a 3-time champ, and also in the 88 games, there was no 4-time champion either.
*   **February 22-March 5, 2021**: Executive producer [Mike Richards](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Mike_Richards "Mike Richards") served as interim host. Richards is the only interim host to be introduced as "The executive producer of _Jeopardy!_," instead of the "The guest host of _Jeopardy!_" 
    *   **February 24, 2021**: First all-male game in the post-Trebek era.

## March 2021[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D9&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **March 8-August 13, 2021**: _Jeopardy!_ matches the total won by the contestants, donating it to a charity of each interim host's and hostess's choice, during their respective episodes.
*   **March 8-19, 2021**: Journalist and author [Katie Couric](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Katie_Couric "Katie Couric") hosted, raising $230,504 for the Pancreatic Cancer Dream Team from Stand Up to Cancer. 
    *   **March 19, 2021**: [Jilana Cotter](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Jilana_Cotter "Jilana Cotter") finishes second with $25,201.

*   **March 22-April 2, 2021**: _The Doctor Oz Show_ host and 2012 _Jeopardy! Power Players Week_ contestant [Dr. Mehmet Oz](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Dr._Mehmet_Oz "Dr. Mehmet Oz") hosted, and raising $268,701 for HealthCorps, Inc _._
    *   **March 22, 2021**: [Nick Cascone](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Nick_Cascone "Nick Cascone") finishes with a 1-day total of $26,801.

## April 2021[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D10&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **April 5-16, 2021**: Now-former quarterback of the Green Bay Packers and 2015 _Celebrity Jeopardy!_ winner [Aaron Rodgers](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") hosted, raising $236,725 for North Valley Community Foundation.
*   **April 19-30, 2021**: _Anderson Cooper 360°_ anchor, 2010 _Celebrity Jeopardy!_ contestant, and 2004 and 2012 _Jeopardy! Power Players Week_ winner and 2016 _Jeopardy! Power Players Week_ contestant [Anderson Cooper](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Anderson_Cooper "Anderson Cooper") hosted, raising $118,000 for Albert Schweitzer Hospital in Haiti and $138,197 for Justice Defenders, with a total of $256,197. 
    *   **April 20, 2021**: _Jeopardy!_ and _Wheel of Fortune_ do not air due to president Joe Biden's speech regarding the George Floyd verdict.
    *   **April 21, 2021**: Max Nupen is the first contestant in the post Trebek era to be disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round with -$1,800.
    *   **April 28, 2021**: [Hari Parameswaran](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Hari_Parameswaran "Hari Parameswaran") finishes third with $0.

## May 2021[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D11&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **May 3-14, 2021**: _60 Minutes_ correspondent [Bill Whitaker](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Bill_Whitaker "Bill Whitaker") hosted, raising $257,998 for Media Fellowship House. 
    *   **May 4, 2021**: [Emily Sands](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Emily_Sands "Emily Sands") finishes with a 3-day total of $73,000. 
        *   First all-female game in the post-Trebek era.

*   **May 6, 2021**: Kalee Hernandez is the first woman contestant in the post-Trebek era to be disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round with -$200.
*   **May 17-28, 2021**: The Tournament of Champions is held, hosted by former _Jeopardy!_ contestant and 2017 Tournament of Champions champion [Buzzy Cohen](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Buzzy_Cohen "Buzzy Cohen"), with the $250,000 grand prize was matched and donated to the _Hope of the Valley Rescue Mission Trebek Center for the Homeless_, now known as and is the first post-Trebek tournament. 
    *   **May 21, 2021**: A tribute is made to honor the late [Brayden Smith](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Brayden_Smith "Brayden Smith"), who tragically died February 5, 2021 exactly one month after the airdate of his last episode.
    *   [Sam Kavanaugh](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Sam_Kavanaugh "Sam Kavanaugh") won the Tournament of Champions and $250,000, the first Tournament of Champions winner after Alex Trebek's death. [Jennifer Quail](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Jennifer_Quail "Jennifer Quail") received $100,000 and [Veronica Vichit-Vadakan](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Veronica_Vichit-Vadakan "Veronica Vichit-Vadakan") received $50,000.
    *   The final one-day total of the finals started to be displayed on the score board before the final two-day match started.
    *   It is the last tournament to use the subtitles 'semifinalist or finalist'. Starting next tournament, the subtitles will be changed from 'semifinalist or finalist' to 'Advance to semifinals or finals'.
    *   It is also the last Tournament of Champions to use the two-day total point affair. Starting with the next Tournament of Champions, the finals will use a best-of-seven series.

*   **May 31-June 11, 2021**: Actress and neuroscientist [Mayim Bialik](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Mayim_Bialik "Mayim Bialik") hosted, raising $194,851 for National Alliance on Mental Illness.

## June 2021[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D12&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **June 14-25, 2021**: NBC's _Today_ co-anchor [Savannah Guthrie](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Savannah_Guthrie "Savannah Guthrie") hosted, raising $217,985 for The Bowery Mission.
*   **June 28-July 9, 2021**: CNN chief medical correspondent [Sanjay Gupta](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Sanjay_Gupta "Sanjay Gupta") hosted, raising $231,059 for Odyssey Atlanta. 
    *   **June 28, 2021**: [Courtney Shah](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Courtney_Shah "Courtney Shah") makes her _Jeopardy!_ debut.
    *   **July 2, 2021**: This is the last episode there the GEICO logo appears in the contestant lectern score displays.

## July 2021[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D13&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **July 5, 2021**: The GEICO logo no longer appears in the contestant lectern score displays, and Johnny reverts to saying "Promotional consideration provided by" before the fee plugs.
*   **July 7, 2021**: [Courtney Shah](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Courtney_Shah "Courtney Shah") finishes with a 7-day total of $118,558, where she is defeated by Nikole Villaneuva in a come from behind win. It makes her the first female champion who won at least five games in the post-Trebek era and the first since [MacKenzie Jones](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/MacKenzie_Jones "MacKenzie Jones") from Season 36.
*   **July 12-August 13, 2021**: The celebrities now serve as interim host for one week only.
*   **July 12-16, 2021**: _Good Morning America_ co-anchor, _This Week_ host, and former democratic advisor [George Stephanopoulos](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/George_Stephanopoulos "George Stephanopoulos") hosted, raising $147,396 for Share Our Strength's No Kid Hungry campaign.
*   **July 19-23, 2021**: _Good Morning America_ co-anchor, former _ESPN_ _SportsCenter_ anchor, and 1999 _Celebrity Jeopardy!_ contestant [Robin Roberts](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Robin_Roberts "Robin Roberts") hosted, raising $164,410 for Be The Match. 
    *   **July 21, 2021**: [Josh Saak](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Josh_Saak "Josh Saak") finishes with a 3-day total of $66,405 and [Matt Amodio](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Amodio "Matt Amodio") makes his _Jeopardy!_ debut by defeating him.
    *   **July 22, 2021**: Pete Wisniewski is disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round with -$400.

*   **July 26-30, 2021**: _Star Trek: The Next Generation_ and _Roots_ actor, former _Reading Rainbow_ host, and 1995 _Celebrity Jeopardy!_ winner [LeVar Burton](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/LeVar_Burton "LeVar Burton") hosted, raised $204,800 for Reading Is Fundamental. 
    *   **July 26, 2021**: Patrick Pearce had -$7,400 at the end of the _Double Jeopardy!_ round, setting the record for the lowest score since the March 12, 2015 episode (#7024), where contestant Stephanie Hull finished the _Double Jeopardy!_ round with -$6,800. So, he was disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round with -$7,400.
    *   **July 29, 2021**: Bryan Cracchiolo is disqualified from playing Final Jeopardy! due to finishing the Double Jeopardy! round with -$1,200. He is the last contestant to be disqualified before Stage 10 was renamed to the Alex Trebek stage.

## August 2021[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fjeopardyhistory.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FJeopardy%21_Timeline_%28syndicated_version%29%2FSeason_37%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D14&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

*   **August 2-6, 2021**: Co-host of CNBC's _Squawk on the Street_ and 2012 _Jeopardy! Power Players Week_ winner [David Faber](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/David_Faber "David Faber") hosted, raising $154,000 for Robin Hood Foundation _._
    *   **August 4, 2021**: [Matt Amodio](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Amodio "Matt Amodio") set the record for the second highest money lost on _Final Jeopardy!_ with $37,000.

*   **August 9-13, 2021:** Fox Sports announcer and sportscaster [Joe Buck](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Joe_Buck "Joe Buck") hosted, raising $159,601 for KidSmart. This also makes the only season have the most hosts of the show, with 17 different hosts. [Joe Buck](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Joe_Buck "Joe Buck") later hosts ESPN Jeopardy! in 2026. 
    *   **August 12, 2021**: [Matt Amodio](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Amodio "Matt Amodio") surpasses [Jason Zuffranieri](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Jason_Zuffranieri "Jason Zuffranieri") as the third-highest winner in regular-season play.
    *   **August 13, 2021**: Season 37 ends, which marked the last episode with the post-credits dedication to Alex Trebek, and the last episode to use the 2008-2021 theme since Season 25, and also the last one to have the promotional fee plugs shown at the conclusion of the game. [Rowan Ward](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Rowan_Ward "Rowan Ward") finishes third with $0. This episode is also [Matt Amodio](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Amodio "Matt Amodio")'s 18th game. 
        *   The guest host and hostess format ended that day. [Mike Richards](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Mike_Richards "Mike Richards") was originally going to be the new host for Season 38, but stepped down after the first week of Season 38, [Ken Jennings](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Ken_Jennings "Ken Jennings") and [Mayim Bialik](https://jeopardyhistory.fandom.com/wiki/Mayim_Bialik "Mayim Bialik") shared hosting duties until 2023.

_**The View**_ is an American [talk show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_show "Talk show") that was created by broadcast journalist [Barbara Walters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Walters "Barbara Walters") and TV producer [Bill Geddie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Geddie "Bill Geddie"). As of 2026[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_View&action=edit), now in its 30th season, the show has aired on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") as part of the network's [daytime programming block](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Daytime "ABC Daytime") since August 11, 1997. The show features a multi-generational panel of women, who discuss the day's "Hot Topics", such as sociopolitical and entertainment news. In addition to the conversation segments, the panel also conducts interviews with prominent figures, such as celebrities and politicians. Production of the show was held in ABC Television Studio 23 in New York City until 2014, when it relocated to the adjacent ABC Broadcast Center, where it stayed until September 2024, when production relocated to ABC Studio B, also in New York City.

Throughout its entire run, _The View_ has had 24 permanent "co-hosts" of varying characteristics and ideologies, with the number of contracted permanent co-hosts ranging between four and eight women per season. The original panel comprised Walters, broadcast journalist [Meredith Vieira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meredith_Vieira "Meredith Vieira"), lawyer [Star Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Jones "Star Jones"), television host [Debbie Matenopoulos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Matenopoulos "Debbie Matenopoulos"), and comedian [Joy Behar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_Behar "Joy Behar"). The current lineup consists of Behar, entertainer [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg"), lawyer [Sunny Hostin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Hostin "Sunny Hostin"), television host [Sara Haines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Haines "Sara Haines"), television personality [Ana Navarro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ana_Navarro "Ana Navarro"), and political strategist [Alyssa Farah Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyssa_Farah_Griffin "Alyssa Farah Griffin"). In addition, the show often makes use of male and female guest panelists.

_The View_ has won [Daytime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytime_Emmy_Awards "Daytime Emmy Awards"), including [Outstanding Talk Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Talk_Show "Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Talk Show"), [Outstanding Informative Talk Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Talk_Show_Informative "Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Talk Show Informative"), and [Outstanding Talk Show Host](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Talk_Show_Host "Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Talk Show Host"). The show has received praise from the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press"), _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_, the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_, _[Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate\_(magazine) "Slate (magazine)")_, as well as _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, which deemed it "the most important political TV show in America". Beginning in its tenth season, the series became subject to on-air controversies and media criticism involving its panel. It was transferred from the helm of ABC's entertainment division to that of [ABC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States) "ABC News (United States)") in 2014 following a decline in ratings. By 2021, _The View_ had become the most-viewed news and talk program in daytime television.

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_View&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Format")]

The original opening credits for _The View_ featured a [voice-over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice-over "Voice-over") from the show's creator and executive producer, [broadcast journalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_journalist "Broadcast journalist")[Barbara Walters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Walters "Barbara Walters"), explaining the show's premise as well as its co-hosts' credentials:

> I've always wanted to do a show with women of different generations, backgrounds, and views: a working mother (broadcast journalist [Meredith Vieira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meredith_Vieira "Meredith Vieira")); a professional in her 30s (lawyer [Star Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Jones "Star Jones")); a young woman just starting out (television host [Debbie Matenopoulos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Matenopoulos "Debbie Matenopoulos")); and then somebody who's done almost everything and will say almost anything (comedian [Joy Behar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_Behar "Joy Behar")). And in a perfect world, I'd get to join the group whenever I wanted...[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-2)

Walters described it as "a talk show featuring four or five women 'of different backgrounds, different generations, and different opinions,' who would discuss the topics of the day, mixing humor with intelligent debate".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-VanityFair-3) The show begins with a segment that features the panel engaging in a discussion pertaining to subjects ranging from politics to social issues as well as pop culture, commonly referred to as "Hot Topics".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-WhoopiView-5) Every episode features multiple "Hot Topics" segments, which take up to most–if not all–of the day's show.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-comeback-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-auto-7) The discussions are frequently followed by interviews with guests.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-WSJ-8) The show also periodically conducts audience giveaways, which often accompanies [deal-of-the-day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deal-of-the-day "Deal-of-the-day") presentations for the home audience under the branding of _View Your Deal_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-9) Every broadcast concludes with the closing remarks: "Have a great day, everyone, and take a little time to enjoy the view."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-10)

The 12th season of _The View_ heavily focused on the events surrounding the [2008 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election "2008 United States presidential election") and featured politicians [John McCain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain "John McCain"), [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton"), and [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") as guests.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-VanityFair-3)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-11) Its 13th season saw the introduction of male guest moderators; among them were television personality [Tom Bergeron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Bergeron "Tom Bergeron"), actor [D. L. Hughley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._L._Hughley "D. L. Hughley"), journalist [Bryant Gumbel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryant_Gumbel "Bryant Gumbel"), and television host [Joe Scarborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Scarborough "Joe Scarborough").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-The_View_Blog-12) Male personalities have since begun serving as guests more frequently, specifically on Fridays, dubbed "Guy Day Friday".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-14) In 2013, the show was speculated to be "trying to become less political".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-15) It began refocusing on politics leading to the [2016 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election") and has reincorporated it back into "Hot Topics" discussions since.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-comeback-6)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-16) During the 25th season, the series introduced weekly episodes that each feature a former co-host as a guest, titled "Flashback Fridays".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-17)

### Seasons 1–10 (1997–2007)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_View&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Seasons 1–10 (1997–2007)")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Barbara_Walters.jpg/250px-Barbara_Walters.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barbara_Walters.jpg)

Broadcast journalist [Barbara Walters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Walters "Barbara Walters") created the series and co-hosted it from 1997 to 2014.

_The View_ premiered with four co-hosts: Meredith Vieira as moderator, Star Jones, Debbie Matenopoulos, and Barbara Walters.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-nytimes-18) Joy Behar, who filled in as the fourth co-host when Walters was unavailable, soon became a full-time co-host.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-19) The five women were the first group that auditioned for the panel, with Behar describing them as having immediately clicked.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-20) Following Matenopoulos's firing in December 1998, broadcast journalist [Lisa Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Ling "Lisa Ling") was brought on as a new co-host in 1999.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-Slate-22) Ling departed the show in December 2002 to host the series _[National Geographic Explorer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Geographic\_Explorer "National Geographic Explorer")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-Slate-22) Former _[Survivor: The Australian Outback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survivor:\_The\_Australian\_Outback "Survivor: The Australian Outback")_ castaway [Elisabeth Hasselbeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisabeth_Hasselbeck "Elisabeth Hasselbeck") replaced Ling beginning November 24, 2003, after Hasselbeck, television personality [Rachel Campos-Duffy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Campos-Duffy "Rachel Campos-Duffy"), and actress [Erin Hershey Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erin_Hershey_Presley "Erin Hershey Presley") each received a week-long on-air tryout.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-24)

In 2006, Vieira left the show to become co-anchor of the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") morning program _[Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today\_(American\_TV\_program) "Today (American TV program)")_;[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-25) her final episode aired on June 9.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-26) That same month, Jones also left the show. Her departure, originally scheduled for July, was brought forward by Walters, publicly feeling "betrayed" by Jones for unexpectedly announcing her departure two days ahead of schedule.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-27) She also said ABC executives had decided not to renew Jones's contract due to diminished approval for Jones through their market research.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-28) Jones later claimed the decision to leave was not hers and that producers informed her that they would not be renewing her contract in April.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-29)

During the [33rd Daytime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Daytime_Emmy_Awards "33rd Daytime Emmy Awards") in April 2006, entertainer [Rosie O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_O'Donnell "Rosie O'Donnell") was introduced as a co-host for the show's tenth season;[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-30) she made her debut on September 5.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-31) After a string of controversies O'Donnell left the show in April 2007 due to failed renewal negotiations.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-rosie07-32) The following month, ABC stated that O'Donnell had asked to be let out of her contract three weeks before its expiration and that she had been granted permission to depart immediately.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-breakup-33)

### Seasons 11–18 (2007–2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_View&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Seasons 11–18 (2007–2015)")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/Mullen_on_The_View.jpg/330px-Mullen_on_The_View.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mullen_on_The_View.jpg)

The co-hosts interview U.S. Navy Adm. [Michael Mullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Mullen "Michael Mullen") and his wife, Deborah, on November 24, 2010.

In August 2007, Walters replaced O'Donnell with actress [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") for season 11.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-WhoopiView-5) Goldberg debuted during the season premiere on September 4.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-34) Actress [Sherri Shepherd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherri_Shepherd "Sherri Shepherd") joined as a permanent co-host beginning September 10.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-35) Hasselbeck went on [maternity leave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maternity_leave "Maternity leave") from October 2007 to January 2008 and again from August to October 2009, with rotating guest co-hosts filling in during the latter.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-39) In August 2009, Walters, Behar, Hasselbeck, Goldberg, and Shepherd won the [Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Talk Show Host](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Talk_Show_Host "Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Talk Show Host").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-Hosts-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-Hosts2-41) Walters took a hiatus after undergoing open-heart surgery in May 2010 and returned on September 7 during the season 14 premiere broadcast.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-43)

In 2013, Behar left the series at the end of season 16.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-Deadline_Hollywood_Behar_Leaving-44) That same month, Hasselbeck was reported to be departing alongside Behar due to market research finding both of their views too "polarizing", which Walters denied.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-THR_Hasselbeck_departing-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-THRHasselbeck-46) Despite Walters' earlier denial, Hasselbeck indeed departed the show on July 10 to join the [Fox News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News "Fox News") morning program _[Fox & Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox\_&\_Friends "Fox & Friends")_.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-47) Behar's final episode, a _[This Is Your Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Is\_Your\_Life\_(American\_franchise) "This Is Your Life (American franchise)")_-style tribute to her, aired on August 9.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-48) Actress [Jenny McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenny_McCarthy "Jenny McCarthy") became a co-host the following season and debuted on its premiere broadcast on September 9.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-49)

Walters retired on May 16, 2014.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-goodbye-51) Shepherd and McCarthy departed the following month and made their final appearances on August 11.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-53)

After making guest appearances during the previous season, actress [Rosie Perez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_Perez "Rosie Perez") as well as former [White House Communications Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Communications_Director "White House Communications Director")[Nicolle Wallace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolle_Wallace "Nicolle Wallace") permanently joined the series in its 18th season,[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-54) establishing Perez as the series' first [Latina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") co-host;[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-55) the two debuted alongside O'Donnell, who permanently returned, and Goldberg during the season premiere on September 15, 2014.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-56) Perez took a hiatus at the end of the year to rehearse for her role in the play _[Fish in the Dark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish\_in\_the\_Dark "Fish in the Dark")_ and returned on February 3, 2015.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-57) That same month, representatives for O'Donnell confirmed that she would once again exit the panel due to "personal reasons"; her final appearance aired on February 12.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-58) Actress [Raven-Symoné](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven-Symon%C3%A9 "Raven-Symoné") joined the series full-time in June after frequently guest co-hosting,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-59) and the following month, comedian [Michelle Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Collins_(comedian) "Michelle Collins (comedian)"), who had been a frequent guest, was permanently added for the following season.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-60) Perez and Wallace exited at the conclusion of the 18th season in August.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-62)

### Seasons 19–30 (2015–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_View&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Seasons 19–30 (2015–present)")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Whoopi_Goldberg_in_2024_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Whoopi_Goldberg_in_2024_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Whoopi_Goldberg_in_2024_(cropped).jpg)

Entertainer [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") has co-hosted and moderated the series since 2007.

The 19th season saw the return of Behar as well as the addition of actress [Candace Cameron Bure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candace_Cameron_Bure "Candace Cameron Bure") and broadcast journalist [Paula Faris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Faris "Paula Faris") as co-hosts alongside Goldberg, Raven-Symoné, and Collins,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-nineteen-63) the lattermost of whom departed in June 2016.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-64) The following season began with eight rotating co-hosts: Behar, Goldberg, Raven-Symoné, Bure, Faris, television host [Sara Haines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Haines "Sara Haines"), lawyer [Sunny Hostin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Hostin "Sunny Hostin"), and television personality [Jedediah Bila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jedediah_Bila "Jedediah Bila").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-Variety-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-Bure-66) Additionally, Behar began moderating on Fridays in Goldberg's place.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-67) On October 27, Raven-Symoné left the show to star in a [spin-off of the sitcom _That's So Raven_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven's_Home "Raven's Home").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-68) On December 8, Bure left the program, citing the commute between coasts and her commitments to other television projects as reasons;[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-Bure-66) her final episode as co-host aired the following day.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-farewell-69)

While Goldberg initially considered leaving after season 20,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-Variety-65) she remained as moderator for season 21, with Behar, Faris, Haines, Hostin, and Bila all returning as co-hosts.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-TheView21-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-71) On September 18, 2017, Bila exited the show on air.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-72) Television personality [Meghan McCain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meghan_McCain "Meghan McCain") subsequently joined the show after leaving her position at Fox News,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-73) debuting as co-host on October 9.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-74) After giving birth to a daughter in December 2017, Haines returned from maternity leave in March 2018.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-75) Faris departed in July.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-76) In the same month, Haines left the show to co-host ABC's new third hour of its morning program _[Good Morning America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good\_Morning\_America "Good Morning America")_;[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-77) she made her final appearance during the season's penultimate broadcast on August 2.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-78)

Broadcast journalist [Abby Huntsman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abby_Huntsman "Abby Huntsman") joined the panel in season 22, making her debut during the season premiere on September 4, 2018.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-79) Following an absence due to the death of [her father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain "John McCain"), McCain returned on October 8.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-80) Television personality [Ana Navarro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ana_Navarro "Ana Navarro") joined the show as a weekly guest co-host the following month.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-NavarroVariety-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-best-82) Goldberg began a hiatus from co-hosting on February 7, 2019, due to pneumonia and sepsis, and returned on March 14.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-84) Huntsman took maternity leave beginning in May.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-86) Behar, Goldberg, Hostin, McCain, and Huntsman all returned for the 23rd season, which premiered on September 3.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-87) In January 2020, Huntsman departed to become a senior advisor to [her father's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Huntsman_Jr. "Jon Huntsman Jr.")[2020 Utah gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Utah_gubernatorial_election "2020 Utah gubernatorial election") campaign;[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-88) she made her final appearance as co-host on January 17.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-89)

Haines returned as a guest co-host beginning in March 2020 and permanently rejoined the panel at the launch of the 24th season.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-studio-92) McCain gave birth to a daughter in September 2020 and returned in January 2021 after a three-month maternity leave.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-94) After four years on the series, McCain departed at the end of the 24th season.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-95) She attributed her decision to her desire to raise her daughter in Washington D.C., to which she had relocated.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-96) McCain later cited the "toxic, direct and purposeful hostility" she experienced at the show as the reason for her exit.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-97) In April 2022, Goldberg took an extended hiatus from co-hosting to film the [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video") series _[Anansi Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anansi\_Boys\_(TV\_series) "Anansi Boys (TV series)")_.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-98) Starting in season 26, Navarro, who has been a weekly guest co-host since 2018, and political strategist [Alyssa Farah Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyssa_Farah_Griffin "Alyssa Farah Griffin") joined the show permanently. With the additions, the panel comprises six co-hosts.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-99)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_View&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Production")]

During its first 17 seasons, _The View_ was filmed in ABC Television Studio 23 in New York City.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-100) The original set for the first four seasons was a leftover set from canceled soap opera _[The City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_City\_(1995\_TV\_series) "The City (1995 TV series)")_.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-102) The panelists conduct discussions around a table or on a sofa and wear [IFB earpieces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interruptible_foldback "Interruptible foldback") through which producers communicate with them.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-WSJ-8)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-103)[Bill Geddie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Geddie "Bill Geddie"), Barbara Walters' longtime producing partner, and Mark Gentile respectively served as showrunner and director for 17 years.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-VanityFair-3)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-105) Walters remained an executive producer until her death.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-106)

_The View_'s 18th season brought significant changes in a "creative overhaul" as well as a "new direction" for the show.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-revamp-107) In August 2014, ABC named [Bill Wolff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Wolff_(television_executive) "Bill Wolff (television executive)"), who had served as vice president of primetime programming at [MSNBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSNBC "MSNBC") and as executive producer of the news and opinion program _[The Rachel Maddow Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rachel\_Maddow\_Show "The Rachel Maddow Show")_, the new executive producer, replacing Bill Geddie.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-108) Production of the show relocated to the ABC Broadcast Center on the [Upper West Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_West_Side "Upper West Side") of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-revamp-107)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-109) During the season premiere on September 15, 2014, the series unveiled its new studio featuring a coffee table-style desk with low-arm chairs, a large video wall, in-the-round audience seating, and an on-camera social media station.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-110) Subsequent tweaks included a glass desk and high stools at center stage,[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-111) as well as color adjustments in backgrounds and graphics.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-113)

In October 2014, ABC shifted production oversight on _The View_ from ABC's [daytime entertainment division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Daytime "ABC Daytime") to [Lincoln Square Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Square_Productions "Lincoln Square Productions"), an [ABC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States) "ABC News (United States)") subsidiary, where the show would be grouped under the division's non-fiction programming umbrella.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-vty-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-nyt-abcnewsview-115) The move allowed the show to leverage ABC News' resources toward news-related segments.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-116) In August 2015, former late-night talk show _[Late Show with David Letterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Show\_with\_David\_Letterman "Late Show with David Letterman")_ producer [Brian Teta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Teta "Brian Teta") joined the show as co-executive producer.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-117) Later in the month, executive producer Wolff departed the show.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-118) In February 2016, along with the show's 20th season renewal, [Candi Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candi_Carter "Candi Carter") was promoted to executive producer after serving as interim showrunner for season 19, becoming the first African-American executive producer in the show's history.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-showrunner-119)

During the 20th-season premiere on September 6, 2016, the show debuted an updated set design with muted colors,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-121) retooled opening titles with footage of the co-hosts in a loft-like space,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-122) as well as a new theme song entitled "World's Gone Crazy", written by [Diane Warren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Warren "Diane Warren") and performed by [Mary J. Blige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_J._Blige "Mary J. Blige").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-123)[Hilary Estey McLoughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilary_Estey_McLoughlin "Hilary Estey McLoughlin") was named senior executive producer in January 2017 after she was brought on as a consultant for season 19.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-124) In September, Teta was promoted to executive producer ahead of the 21st-season premiere.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-TheView21-70) Sarah de la O serves as director, as of September 2019.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-back-125) In March 2020, the series began airing without a live studio audience as a precaution in light of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-126) Carter departed that same month to become the showrunner of the daytime talk show _[Tamron Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamron\_Hall\_(talk\_show) "Tamron Hall (talk show)")_.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-127) During the pandemic, the co-hosts broadcast from different locations, with Joy Behar, Whoopi Goldberg, Sunny Hostin, Meghan McCain, and Ana Navarro filming remotely, while Sara Haines remained in the studio, where Teta also still produced.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-128)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-129) McLoughlin exited in February 2021.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-130)

For the series' 25th season, which began in September 2021, the co-hosts returned to filming in front of a live studio audience for the first time since March 2020.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-131) The show also presented a new theme song entitled "For My Girls", written by Warren and performed by [Brandy Norwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandy_Norwood "Brandy Norwood") and [Nicole Scherzinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Scherzinger "Nicole Scherzinger").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-132)

For the series' 28th season, which premiered on September 3, 2024, _The View_ relocated from the ABC Broadcast Center to Studio B of Disney's new [7 Hudson Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_Hudson_Square "7 Hudson Square") headquarters in Manhattan, serving as the first production to move to the new facility. The new studio extensively uses video walls along the walls and floors, allowing for more "dynamic" redressing of the entire set with different scenery using graphics. The existing desk was brought to the new studio, and was described as being the "jumping-off point" of the new studio's look and feel.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-134)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-135) The show also debuted a new theme song entitled "This Version", written by Warren and performed by [Leona Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leona_Lewis "Leona Lewis").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-136)

## Notable episodes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_View&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Notable episodes")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Barack_Obama_guests_on_The_View.jpg/330px-Barack_Obama_guests_on_The_View.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barack_Obama_guests_on_The_View.jpg)

The co-hosts interview [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"), President of the United States, on July 29, 2010.

In 2010, U.S. President Barack Obama appeared as a guest on the show during the July 29 broadcast, marking the first appearance on a daytime talk show by a sitting U.S. president.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-137) The episode also saw the return of Barbara Walters following her open heart surgery in May before she resumed her hiatus.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-138) On February 22, 2012, Star Jones came on as a guest and discussed her contentious exit from the show, marking her first appearance since said exit in 2006.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-CBS_News_Star_Jones_returns-139) On February 7, 2014, Rosie O'Donnell returned as a guest for the first time since quitting the show in 2007.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-140) All eleven co-hosts in the show's history appeared during Walters' penultimate episode as co-host on May 15 to celebrate her retirement.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-141) Walters' final appearance as co-host aired the following day; it featured several guests, including Hillary Clinton and television host [Oprah Winfrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oprah_Winfrey "Oprah Winfrey").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-goodbye-51)

On March 27, 2015, the show celebrated its 4,000th broadcast, with Walters and Joy Behar returning for the celebration.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-View4000-142) On September 5, 2016, prior to the premiere of Season 20, ABC aired a documentary entitled _The View: 20 Years in the Making_, which featured notable moments from the show and several personalities involved in its history, hosted by Behar.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-143) On November 8, Behar, Jedediah Bila, Candace Cameron Bure, Sara Haines, and Sunny Hostin hosted a primetime [Election Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_elections "2016 United States elections") special of the show, which aired on [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)").[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-144) On November 11, the series aired a "Flashback Friday" episode, which featured the original panel of co-hosts comprising Behar, Jones, Meredith Vieira, and Debbie Matenopoulos as well as a Veteran's Day tribute.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-secret-145)

In March 2017, the show had its first remote broadcast from [Walt Disney World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_World "Walt Disney World") in [Orlando, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida").[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-146) Five episodes were filmed in front of the [Tree of Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_of_Life_(Disney) "Tree of Life (Disney)") at [Disney's Animal Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney's_Animal_Kingdom "Disney's Animal Kingdom"), featuring pre-recorded segments with Behar, Bila, Haines, Hostin, Paula Faris, and Whoopi Goldberg exploring [Epcot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epcot "Epcot"), [Magic Studios").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View#cite_note-147) Film director [James Cameron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cameron "James Cameron") came on as a guest on March 9, giving
